trust_decision.summary: Whether an MCP server config (command/args/env/url) loaded from a workspace file (<ws>/.amazonq/mcp.json or .amazonq/agents/default.json) may be spawned without user consent; at the pinned commit there is no decision at all, and McpManager.initOneServerInternal spawns every loaded server. The fix adds a gate there that treats any __configPath__ not equal to one of the three global paths as workspace-scoped and needs a persisted approval or a prompt.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'arbitrary code execution'. The only process spawn from workspace MCP config is StdioClientTransport in initOneServerInternal, and that function is also the single chokepoint where the published gate lands.

fix_sites.entry_point: LSP initialize -> toolServer MCP init -> McpManager.discoverAllServers -> initOneServer (also addServer/addRegistryServer/updateServer/updateServerPermission from MCP UI events)
fix_sites.module_kind: core manager (consent gate inserted at top of initOneServerInternal, fix.diff:471-530)

fix_sites.entry_point: new internal module mcpConsentStore (hasApproval/recordApproval/removeApproval), called only from the gate
MCP UI 'delete server' -> McpManager.removeServer (approval cleanup, fix.diff:687-691)
McpManager.close / reinitializeMcpServers (clear session deny cache, fix.diff:539)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: fix.diff:168-283 (new mcpConsentStore persisted approvals file; read through hasApproval at fix.diff:250-261, later OR-matched at fix.diff:630)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue that a session-only prompt meets 'ask before running workspace servers', and that persisting approvals across reloads (keyed on name, config fingerprint and workspace) is a UX feature, not part of the security fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Servers from the global configs (~/.aws/amazonq/mcp.json, agents/default.json, personas/default.json) must keep starting with no prompt. An approved workspace server must start silently after a reload. A workspace server that overrides a global one by name becomes workspace-scoped.

O6_input_shapes: remote server (url+headers), also gated (fingerprint includes url, fix.diff:205)
config from workspace .amazonq/agents/default.json (manual and registry entries)
__configPath__ given as a file: URI rather than an fs path (normalized in the second commit, fix.diff:677-679)

O7_producer.where: server/aws-lsp-codewhisperer/src/language-server/agenticChat/tools/mcp/mcpUtils.ts:527 (and :134, :473) sets __configPath__, which the gate trusts to decide global vs workspace

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The published fingerprint leaves out __additionalEnv__ and headers/__additionalHeaders__. A workspace agent's registry entry env is merged into the spawn env, so an env-only change to an approved server does not change the fingerprint or the deny key.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Registry-mode servers come from an org-controlled registry, and the extra env is shown as a separate 'additional' UI field, so it looks like user-supplied tuning rather than server identity.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: producer in mcpUtils.ts; it reaches the spawn env at mcpManager.ts:429; fingerprint in new mcpConsentStore.ts (fix.diff:200-208)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Make the gate's identity/fingerprint use cfg.env only, while the spawn merges __additionalEnv__ (a coupled hidden value next to the fingerprinted one).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: __additionalEnv__ is a separate 'runtime-only' field added for registry servers (mcpTypes.ts:42). A maintainer who writes the fingerprint from the declared schema fields would naturally skip the double-underscore internals.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The global-vs-workspace decision compares __configPath__ strings exactly. Path variants (file: URI, un-normalized '..', case on Windows) of a workspace path, or a workspace path built differently by loadAgentConfig (path.normalize at :279) versus the gate, decide trust differently.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two path builders already exist (normalizePathFromUri vs path.normalize(URI.fsPath)), and the second published commit had to add normalization at the gate, which shows this drift really happens.

O9_family: missing authorization / implicit trust of workspace-supplied configuration leading to process execution (CWE-732 as published; closer to CWE-829/CWE-862)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm workspaces monorepo, tsc, mocha/chai/sinon tests
O10_build.project_tests: server/aws-lsp-codewhisperer/src/language-server/agenticChat/tools/mcp/mcpManager.test.ts (existing, 1900+ lines; the fix appends a consent-gate describe block); mcpConsentStore.test.ts is new in the fix

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Prompt (or refuse) for every server in initOneServerInternal, or only for legacy .amazonq/mcp.json, with no persisted approval, which either breaks global servers and reload-without-reprompt or misses the workspace agent file.

out_of_scope_notes: Trusted global servers are spawned with cwd = the first workspace folder (mcpManager.ts:437-440), so command resolution (e.g. npx/local bin) can pick up workspace content. This is a different property and was not pursued.

The second published commit weakens the first: hasApproval matches on (name AND (fingerprint OR workspaceHash)) (fix.diff:630), so changing an approved server's command inside the same workspace does not re-prompt, and the same name+config in a different workspace is auto-approved. Hidden tests built on the final state would enforce this weaker behaviour.

Task-design caveat (no matching red_flag enum): the published fix is a new feature (a consent store module with specific exports, button title 'Allow for this server', state reason 'consent not granted'). The fix's own tests stub './mcpConsentStore' and call the private initOneServerInternal, so the behavioural tests would have to be rewritten to be API-neutral to stay fair.

Every entry point funnels through one chokepoint (initOneServer -> initOneServerInternal, mcpManager.ts:305, 906, 1046, 1232, 1461), so route count gives WHERE-type room only.
